qualifications: The current evidence is a single popular article and does not specify which tasks are safe to automate or which roles can work offline.
claims.statement: [[WorkHabits]] can include automation for suitable tasks and offline work when network access creates distraction.

qualifications: The source recommends RSS-style tools without comparing outcomes or addressing information-selection errors.
claims.statement: [[AttentionManagement]] can use subscriptions and offline reading to control when information arrives, but delivery format alone does not establish relevance or quality.

summary: Personal productivity practices can use simple tools and environmental controls to reduce avoidable work and distraction, but the current corpus does not establish that automation or disconnection is universally appropriate.
